# Hash tables

## How hash tables work

A hash table stores key-value pairs and finds a value by applying a hash function to its key. The hash function maps a key to an index in an array of buckets. Two different keys can map to the same index, which is called a collision. Chaining resolves collisions by storing all keys that share an index in a linked list.

## Performance

Open addressing resolves collisions by probing for another empty slot in the array. With a good hash function and a low load factor, lookups take constant time on average. As the load factor approaches one, collisions become more frequent and lookups slow down. Most implementations resize the table and rehash every key when the load factor passes a threshold.
